extracted.intended_audience: students or readers of ancient philosophy/ethics (Aristotle)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts Aristotle's account of intellectual and moral faculties (Knowledge, Art, Practical Wisdom, Science, Intuition, Judiciousness, Good Counsel) and the standards by which each is identified and evaluated in moral action and deliberation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function–Excellence (ergon–aretē) principle
rubrics_metrics.description: We must discover the best state of each faculty because that will be the Excellence of each; excellence is relative to the work each has to do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate a faculty by identifying its proper function (work) and then the state in which it performs that function best. This is the general method for defining 'virtue' or 'excellence' across faculties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three faculties bearing on moral action
rubrics_metrics.description: There are in the Soul three functions on which depend moral action and truth; Sense, Intellect, Appetition (vague Desire or definite Will).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish contributions of sense (not the source of moral action), intellect, and appetition when assessing moral responsibility or deliberative capacity; brutes have sense but lack moral action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral Choice as starting-point of moral action
rubrics_metrics.description: The starting-point of moral action is Moral Choice, i.e. Appetition, and Reason directed to a certain result; Moral Choice is Will consequent on deliberation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess moral action by examining whether will and reason align: the Reason must be true and the Will right for good Moral Choice. Moral choice concerns future, influenceable actions, not the past.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberation's domain: future and contingent
rubrics_metrics.description: No one deliberates about things which cannot be otherwise than they are; deliberation concerns the future and matters that may be influenced (contingent matters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat as incorrect any attempt to apply deliberative standards or practical wisdom to necessary truths or past actions; deliberation-related virtues apply only to contingent, actionable situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge (episteme)
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge is 'a state or mental faculty apt to demonstrate syllogistically' and concerns what cannot be otherwise than it is; what comes within the range of Knowledge is by necessity and therefore eternal; it is teachable and learnable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge a claim of knowledge by whether it rests on demonstrative syllogism from principles known to the knower; knowledge deals with necessary, eternal truths and presupposes provable principles (often via induction for first principles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Art (technē)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is 'a certain state of mind, conjoined with true Reason, apt to Make' and has to do with production and contrivance of things which may either be or not be; Art concerns making (production), not doing (action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify abilities as art if they are about producing contingent objects by application of true reason; errors: confusing art with doing/acting or treating natural/necessary phenomena as objects of art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical Wisdom (phronesis / πολιτικὴ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical Wisdom is 'a state of mind true, conjoined with Reason, and apt to Do, having for its object those things which are good or bad for Man' — the capacity to deliberate well about living well and to calculate about ends that have no definite rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate practical wisdom by: ability to deliberate well about human goods, acquaintance with particulars (experience), capacity for appropriate ends and proper means, and being true and conjoined with reason. Practical Wisdom is concerned with doing and is not identical to Knowledge or Art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical Wisdom requires particulars and experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical Wisdom is not merely knowledge of general principles but requires knowledge of particulars and details (those apt to act); men who derive knowledge from actual experience can be more practical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing someone's phronesis, weight experience and detailed, case-level knowledge; younger persons may be Scientific but lack Practical Wisdom because they lack experience of particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science (scientific knowledge) as union of Knowledge and Intuition
rubrics_metrics.description: Science means the most accurate of all Knowledge; the Scientific man must not merely know deductions from first principles but possess truth respecting the First Principles — Science is 'equivalent to Intuition and Knowledge', a union of both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat scientific understanding as highest demonstrative knowledge grounded in grasp of first principles (intuition) plus demonstrative reasoning; distinguishes pure science from practical wisdom because its objects are immutable/necessary rather than human contingent goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intuition (nous) — grasp of first principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Intuition is the faculty which takes in the first principles of Knowledge; it takes in those principles which cannot be proved by reasoning and serves as the beginning and end of demonstrative reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize intuition where someone apprehends first principles directly (undemonstrable dicta); consider the views of experienced and skilled people (the old, the practically wise) as sources of practical intuition in absence of demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good Counsel (right deliberation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Good Counsel is 'Rightness in respect of what conduces to a given End' — a rightness of deliberation apt to attain a good end, neither Knowledge nor Opinion nor Happy Conjecture, but rightness of intellectual operation focused on expedient ends and proper means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess counsel by whether deliberation aims at proper ends, pursues them by right means and right time, and is directed by Practical Wisdom; counsel can be general (toward a general end) or particular (toward a specific end).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judiciousness (synesis/ability to judge suggestions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judiciousness is aptness to decide upon suggestions; it shares object-matter with Practical Wisdom (things one might doubt and deliberate about) but is not the capacity to command or initiate; it consists in employing the opinionative faculty to judge well what another states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish judiciousness from full practical wisdom: judge someone 'judicious' when they can well receive and assess proposals/decisions, but reserve 'practically-wise' for those able to set policy and initiate action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gnome / right judgment (equity-related judgment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The faculty called γνώμη (gnōmē) is 'the right judgment of the equitable man' — a tendency to make allowance, to make equitable decisions; συγγνώμη (allowance) is right γνώμη with capacity for making equitable decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate character by the presence of equitable judgment: ability to make allowance and exercise fairness in judgment denotes this faculty; it aligns with truthful/right disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation of Practical Wisdom and Moral Virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: One cannot be strictly speaking good without Practical Wisdom nor Practically-Wise without moral goodness; Practical Wisdom gives the right means, Moral Virtue gives right aim and direction. Vice distorts moral vision and prevents correct practical principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing moral excellence, require both right moral disposition (virtue) and practical wisdom: moral choice cannot be right independently of both. Practical Wisdom presupposes moral goodness and vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: Making vs Doing (Art vs Action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Making and Doing are different: Art concerns making (production) of things that may be otherwise, whereas Doing concerns action (ends that are ends in themselves); Art deals with production while action's end is within the action itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflating technical skill (art) with practical moral action: assess whether the competence aims at producing objects or at performing actions for their own sake; different standards apply (production-oriented vs action-oriented).

rubrics_metrics.name: Degrees and unity: Art admits degrees; Practical Wisdom does not
rubrics_metrics.description: Art admits of degrees of excellence, and in Art one who goes wrong purposely is preferable to him who does so unwittingly; but Practical Wisdom and other moral virtues do not admit degrees in this way — they are of a different kind (Excellence rather than Art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating excellence, treat technical arts as gradable skills; treat Practical Wisdom and moral virtues as coherent states tied to character, not merely technical proficiency with gradable skill distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin and teachability: teaching presupposes prior knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: All teaching and intellectual learning proceed on the basis of previous knowledge; induction and syllogism are the two ways of teaching (induction produces universals, syllogism reasons from universals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess claims of teachability and learning by whether prior knowledge or exemplars exist; use induction to establish principles and syllogistic demonstration to teach from those principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: First principles and limits of demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: There are first principles which cannot themselves be proved syllogistically; the faculty taking in these first principles cannot be Knowledge, Art, or Practical Wisdom, but is Intuition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the epistemic limit of demonstration: when evaluating arguments, identify their first principles and note whether they are grasped by intuition rather than proved; do not demand syllogistic proof for basic first premises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error sources in practical deliberation
rubrics_metrics.description: In matters of practice, error attaches either to the general rule (process of deliberation) or to the particular fact (particular mistaken perception).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When diagnosing flawed decisions, check both the general premises/rules used in deliberation and the particular factual beliefs; correct either the rule or the factual judgment as appropriate.
